Safety features are like friends – you can never have too many. And if you’ve
compared Azera to its primary competitors, you already know this: Azera has more
standard passive and active advanced safety features than they do.1
Azera is the only car in its class to offer Blind Spot Detection with Lane Change
Assist and Rear Cross-traffic Alert as standard.2 This radar-based system helps
detect the presence of vehicles in your rear blind spots while driving, and warns of
cars approaching from the side when backing out of parking spaces. Completing the
full circle of technology, Azera Limited's available Forward Collision Warning uses a
forward-sensing camera to monitor for potential collisions and alerts the driver.
At the core of the 2017 Azera’s active safety strategy is an advanced Vehicle
Stability Management system. It automatically manages several important safety
features including Electronic Stability Control with a Traction Control System and an
Anti-lock Braking System with Electronic Brake-force Distribution and Brake Assist.3
All standard.
Hyundai’s award-winning Blue Link® Connected Care system is also standard for the
first year of ownership.4 It includes Enhanced Roadside Assistance, SOS Emergency
Assistance, Monthly Vehicle Health Reports and more – a few very good friends to
have onboard when you need them.
1 Claim based on comparison of specifications on manufacturer websites. 2 Lane Change Assist provides an audible and
visual alert if the turn signal is activated and another vehicle in the blind spot is sensed. There are limitations to the
function, range, detection and clarity of the system. Rear Cross-traffic Alert is active when the vehicle is in reverse gear
and backing at a speed less than 6 mph. It may not detect all vehicles, depending on the size, angle, distance and speed
of the other vehicle, and does not detect stationary objects or slow moving objects near the car, including pedestrians.
See Owner’s Manual for further product details and limitations. 3 Electronic Stability Control (ESC) cannot control your
vehicle’s stability under all driving situations. ESC is not a substitute for safe driving practices. No system, no matter
how advanced, can overcome physics or correct poor driving. The driver is always responsible for controlling the vehicle
and must use caution to avoid loss of control in all driving conditions. Speed, road conditions and driver steering input
will affect whether ESC can help prevent loss of control. See Owner’s Manual for details. The Traction Control System is
meant to enhance conscientious driving habits and is not a substitute for safe driving practices. 4 Blue Link Connected
Care includes one year of the Blue Link Connected Care Package and requires an active Blue Link subscription. One-
year term starts from the new vehicle date of first use and is available for new vehicle purchases and leases based upon
terms and conditions on the Blue Link subscription enrollment pages. Cellular and GPS coverage is required.
